related_issues.title: [FEATURE] Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php grammar
related_issues.relevance: The assigned issue; maintainers implement in-house and external PRs are not accepted (issue Note on Process)

constraints: The grammar entry point is tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (a LanguageFn, .into() to Language); LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY does not accept the <?php tags needed for the HTML-mix edge case, so use LANGUAGE_PHP.
tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 declares dev-dependency tree-sitter 0.27, matching the workspace tree-sitter 0.27.1 pin.
The inheritance clauses have no field names in the grammar, so child_by_field_name('superclass') or ('interfaces') returns None; the Java-style extract_inheritance returns [] for PHP.
variable_name node text includes the leading $; the parser compares captured text to the bare symbol, so the defuse captures must target the inner (name) node.

Imports: the parser's fallback arm in extract_imports_from_node stores the full captured text as module; capturing namespace_use_clause yields the clause text; the group prefix of 'use A\{B, C}' is lost.

EXTENSION_MAP feeds supported_file_ext_pattern() (schema_helpers.rs), so the tool schema pattern gains php automatically; this is a schema-surface change that the issue's 'no schema changes' scope should be aware of.
Cargo.lock new entries must be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md); the GitHub release v0.25.2 is dated 2026-11-19, but the crates.io publish time was not verified in this read-only run.
cargo deny must pass without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK; the tree-sitter-php license is MIT (in the deny.toml allow-list); it adds a cc build dependency.

README intro count is 18 and the list omits Swift; lib.rs (line 23), aptu-coder-core lib.rs (line 11) and aptu-coder-core/README.md (lines 22, 66) also list languages and are stale for Swift; out of the issue's stated README scope.

The DEFUSE_QUERY has no production caller since the symbol tool removal (parser_elements.rs comment before extract_def_use); it is required by the issue's five-constant scope and by parity with java/swift, not by a runtime path.

approaches.name: A: Swift-style handler with LANGUAGE_PHP and child-iteration inheritance (recommended)
approaches.description: Add languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as drafted; extract_inheritance walks named children of kind base_clause and class_interface_clause; wire tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP into get_language_info, get_ts_language, EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages; add Cargo entries and Cargo.lock; add inline tests and one integration test.
pros: Follows the Swift template (#1742) for the wiring and inheritance walk
Handles the HTML-mix edge case because LANGUAGE_PHP accepts php tags
Uses only node kinds and fields confirmed in node-types.json and define-grammar.js
Smallest diff that satisfies every acceptance criterion in the issue
cons: Query text is unverified until a unit test compiles it against LANGUAGE_PHP (no build run in this read-only pass)
Import capture loses the group prefix for grouped use statements
Schema pattern changes because EXTENSION_MAP feeds it

approaches.name: B: Java clone with field-based inheritance (rejected)
approaches.description: Copy java.rs, rename node kinds to PHP, and keep the Java extract_inheritance that reads child_by_field_name('superclass') and 'interfaces' and matches type_identifier.
pros: Reuses the Java test shape exactly
cons: PHP grammar has no superclass or interfaces fields, so extends and implements would come back empty and fail the acceptance criterion
Java type_identifier does not exist in PHP; names are name, qualified_name, relative_name
Would need a second rewrite after the first test failure

approaches.name: C: Drive queries from upstream queries/tags.scm (not recommended)
approaches.description: Reuse tree-sitter-php queries/tags.scm (which captures @name with @definition.function, @definition.class, @reference.call, @reference.class and @reference.implementation) as the basis for the five queries; add a PHP-specific capture mapping in parser_elements.rs.
pros: tags.scm already encodes the variable_name (name) and class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] patterns
cons: Capture names (@name, @definition.*, @reference.*) do not match the aptu consumers (function, class, func_name, method_name, class_name, call, import_path, type_ref), so the shared parser_elements.rs or the handler must change
Touches shared code the issue does not scope (its Scope says handler and registry only)
tags.scm has no import or inheritance-walk patterns

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion without touching shared parser code: LANGUAGE_PHP is the correct entry point, the inheritance walk must be child-iteration (the grammar has no fields for the clauses), and the Swift wiring pattern from #1742 gives the registry changes. Verify the five queries with a unit test that calls Query::new against LANGUAGE_PHP before wiring, as the issue suggests.

(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration

inheritance_walk_citation: Source inspected: tree-sitter-php common/define-grammar.js (the php/grammar.js file is a 3-line require of ../common/define-grammar.js) and php/src/node-types.json. (1) class_declaration (define-grammar.js lines 365-373) has field 'name' (kind name), field 'body' (declaration_list), and optional unfielded children base_clause and class_interface_clause; node-types.json lists no 'superclass' or 'interfaces' field, so child_by_field_name() returns None for both. (2) For the extends clause, iterate the class node's named children and select kind == 'base_clause' (define-grammar.js lines 334-337: keyword('extends') followed by commaSep1($._name)). For each named child of base_clause whose kind is 'name', 'qualified_name' or 'relative_name' (node-types.json base_clause children), push format!("extends {text}") where text is source[start_byte..end_byte]. (3) For the implements clause, select kind == 'class_interface_clause' (define-grammar.js lines 381-384: keyword('implements') followed by commaSep1($._name)) and push format!("implements {text}") for each named child of kinds name/qualified_name/relative_name. (4) Result for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}' is ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for 'class Plain {}' it is []. Java's field-based walk (superclass / interfaces, child kind type_identifier) would return [] for PHP, so the Swift-style child iteration in swift.rs is the correct template. Interface 'extends' lists also use base_clause (interface_declaration children: base_clause), so the same walk yields extends entries for interfaces.
